newsitem.title: FINLAND: Analysts see Huhtamaki acquisitions soon.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Huhtamaki acquisitions soon.

text.p: Huhtamaki Oy will not waste time in using at least some of the 1.5 billion markka it gains through an asset swap with Hershey Foods to develop its core businesses, Finnish analysts said on Friday.
They expect the confectionery and packaging group to announce acquisitions in both areas in the near future.

Analysts welcomed the surprise announcement earlier today that Huhtamaki planned to swap confectionery units with U.S. Hershey but would retain royalty rights, spelling an end to problems in the U.S. and giving it a 1.5 billion markka warchest.
"They can now expand with this money both in Europe and in Asia," one analyst said, requesting anonymity, adding that she expected acquisitions both in confectionery and packaging.

"In my opinion, this is extremely good news. They will get rid of the problems which they have had in the U.S. -- (sweet brand) Jolly Rancher's fall in sales and delays in plant rationalision programmes," she said.
Huhtamaki shares soared on the deal to close at 218.00 markka, their highest since at least 1991, up 33.00 markka or almost 18 percent.
"This was definitely a sensible thing to do," another analyst said, adding that the two companies were probably able to use their relative advantages in local market knowledge.
"Some (acquisition) will surely come pretty soon ... it could even be quite big," he said on condition of anonymity.
After the sale of Leiras and this swap, Huhtamaki has some 2.5 billion markka in cash, compared to its market capitalisation of 6.3 billion markka, he noted.
Huhtamaki CEO Timo Peltola said Huhtamaki had 1.5 billion markka to develop the company after the deal.
